42_marg2664: The words of Amos. Jerome: Amos prophesies, not to Jerusalem, but to Israel in Samaria, as appears from what is written: “And Amasias the priest of Bethel sent to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying: Amos hath rebelled against thee in the midst of the house of Israel.” And a little after, Amaziah said to Amos: “Thou seer, go, flee away into the land of Juda: … and prophesy there. But prophesy not again any more in Bethel: because it is the king's sanctuary, and it is the house of the kingdom.” To whom Amos answered: “I am not a prophet, nor am I the son of a prophet: but I am a herdsman plucking wild figs. And the Lord took me when I followed the flock, and the Lord said to me: Go, prophesy to my people Israel.”
42_interl4656: With that sight by which prophets are called seers, who understood by the Holy Spirit what they prophesied.
42_interl4658: Before Uzziah was struck with leprosy.
42_interl4659: That is, before the captivity shook everything; which, in the two years, shows the twofold distress of the ten tribes and of the two; so that, if they would do penance, they would not feel the earthquake afterwards.
42_marg2665: Uzziah means “the rule” or “the strength of the Lord.” Jeroboam “pointing out,” or “the cause of the people,” or “the division of the people,” or “delay,” or “temporal.” Tekoa “sounding the trumpet”; Amos “torn away.” So at the time when the people was torn away from the Lord, or from the kingdom of David, Amos, like one sounding the trumpet, sang over Israel, which was once most upright before God, while Uzziah reigned in Judea, in whom, because of the temple and the holy of holies, the strength of the Lord remained, and he ruled a people that confessed him. But Jeroboam, who was the cause of the division of the people, reigns in Israel, which serves idols.
42_marg2666: Uzziah is the same as Azariah, who, claiming for himself a priesthood not his due, was struck with leprosy on his forehead; and there was also a great earthquake through all Jerusalem. Jeroboam was the great-grandson of Jehu, to whom the Lord had promised that kings of his seed would be over Israel until the fourth generation; and in this Jeroboam that promise was fulfilled.
42_marg2667: It is natural that all who wish to compare one thing with another should take their comparisons from the things they have experienced and been brought up among. For example, sailors liken their enemies to winds, loss to shipwreck, sorrow to a storm, and joy and prosperity to the calmest breeze, the sea to the plains. So shepherds liken their fear to the roaring of a lion, and call their enemies lions, bears or wolves. So this man, who was a shepherd of flocks, compares the fear of God to the roaring of a lion: he will roar from Sion and utter his voice from Jerusalem, where the temple and the religion of God were, not from Bethel or Dan, where the golden calves were. He will roar, that is, he will strike fear into the ten tribes, threatening captivity; and so the beautiful places of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall be withered. By these is signified the land of the ten tribes, which was most fertile, and which was soon to be taken captive by the Assyrians under Hoshea, their last king, who is signified by the top of Carmel. When he was carried off, the beautiful places of the shepherds, the princes of the world and the mighty of the ten tribes, mourned, because their land was emptied when the king was carried off.
42_interl4661: The greater ones in the people will weep, because Hoshea king of Israel will be crushed and taken captive.
42_marg2668: Allegorically: When God, from the watchtower of the Church, in which is the vision of peace, has uttered his voice through the teachers of the Old and New Testaments, then the beautiful places of the shepherds, namely the teaching of the heretics, which seemed fair and promised the knowledge of the true circumcision, will mourn and be dried up; and the peoples, who for their simplicity are called flocks, will wither in a sudden drought.
42_marg2669: They are the level plains, the green of the pastures, places abounding in divers grasses. There are two mountains called Carmel: one from which came Nabal the Carmelite, the other on which Elijah prayed; and both are very rich in pasture.

42_marg2670: He begins with Damascus because at the time when Amos prophesied, Hazael was grievously afflicting the ten tribes.
42_marg2671: Damascus is the chief city of Syria, which Eliezer, the servant of Abraham, founded in the field where Abel was killed. Gilead is a city and region beyond the Jordan, in the lot of the half tribe of Manasseh. At the time when Amos began to prophesy, Hazael king of Damascus so laid waste that region that, having overcome Ahab king of Israel at Ramoth-gilead, he crushed that whole region like the threshing-sledges that thresh the corn on the floors.
42_interl4665: that is, he crushed Gilead as the corn is beaten out on the floors by wheels shod beneath with iron and teeth, and the straw is crushed for the cattle’s food, for want of hay
42_marg2672: Jerome: Another translation: because they have threshed the women with child of Gilead with iron saws. The women with child are the souls that have lately been made fruitful by the word of God, whom the heretics draw away from the Church and grind with iron teeth like food. For it belongs to the little ones to be scandalized, not to the perfect.
42_marg2673: Allegorically: The first sin is to think evil; the second to consent; the third to fulfil it in deed; the fourth not to repent. He who sins in the first three, if he repents, God turns him to the face of his mercy; but if he does not repent, the face of his mercy is turned away from him.
42_marg2674: Allegorically: Gilead means “the passing over” or “the removal of testimony,” and signifies those who, having passed over from the Church into heresy, carry the testimonies of God they had received before into strange territory. Such as these the heretics crush with wains and iron wheels with teeth; of whom it is said: “The sons of men, whose teeth are weapons and arrows.” For the heretics not only think and do evil, but deceive the simple with wicked teaching and drink their blood: for Damascus means “a drinking of blood.” From such sins the Lord turns away his face, so that those who do not see the truth of the divine teaching, the divine face being turned away, may be overwhelmed with darkness. And when they try to deceive others, the Lord sends a fire into the house which they call Hazael, that is, “the vision of God,” and it devours in them the wood and the stubble, and also the whole house, that is, the structure of their fraud, and besides the bars, that is, the strongest arguments of their art of dialectic. When these are broken, the inhabitants of the plain of the idol are destroyed, that is, idolatry is destroyed; and when it is destroyed, those who seemed to hold the sceptre in it are made of no account; and the lofty and sublime people, which is raised up in pride and promises itself heavenly things, will be led away captive, so that it may be taken and carried over to its own salvation.
42_marg2675: The father of Hazael was called Benadab, with b as the last letter; the son of Hazael was called Benadat, with t. When Hazael died in Syria, while Uzziah and Jeroboam reigned, he succeeded his father in the kingdom; and from him all the kings of Aram, that is, of Syria and Damascus, were afterwards called Ben-hadad, as the Pharaohs from the first Pharaoh and the Caesars from Caesar. So he threatens that he will crush the royal house of Hazael, and his son Ben-hadad. For we read that Tiglath-pileser king of the Assyrians, having overcome Egypt, came and plundered the ten tribes, and afterwards turned to Syria and killed Rezin king of Syria, of whom we read in Isaiah, and carried the people of Syria captive to Cyrene, which is at the furthest borders of Egypt.

42_marg2679: Allegorically: Gaza means “strength” or “rule,” Edom “bloody” or “earthly,” Ashdod “fire of the breast,” Ashkelon “murderous fire,” or “hung up,” or “weighed,” Ekron “barrenness” or “rooting out.” Gaza is accused, which promises itself the strength of its knowledge and rule, because it shuts up captives in Edom. These are the masters of the Jews, who follow not the spirit but the letter, and interpret everything in an earthly way. So a fire is sent into the walls of Gaza, by which all the arguments by which they defend their lies are destroyed. It also consumes the houses, that is, whatever seems built by the art of dialectic; and from Ashdod is cut off the inhabitant who, following the letter, has breasts full not of milk but of fire; and the sceptre is taken from Ashkelon, where is the murderous fire of the devil, which kills whomever it breathes upon, as the fire of God refreshes those it enters. The hand is also turned against Ekron, where is barrenness: for to him who does not receive the spiritual understanding is given “a womb without children, and dry breasts.” Besides, all the rest of the Philistines are destroyed: either the city of Gath, where is the winepress of the devil, or all who fall by the cup. For when they are drunk, they will fall and wallow in their vomit.

42_marg2688: Jerome: This is the difference between the cruelty of the Damascenes and that of the children of Ammon: those crush with iron wains, these rip up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge their border. The Damascenes, who drink blood, signify the heretics, who not only tear new believers from the Church but crush and grind the people of God with iron teeth like bread. Ammon, which means “people of grief” or “my people,” signifies the schismatics, who separate from the Church the untaught souls that had lately conceived the word of God. Yet they do not butcher those they have cut off so cruelly as the heretics; but, remaining in the same rule of faith, they wish to spread the name of their own glory among those who come after. So God threatens that he will burn their fortifications, and that the author of the schism will go captive, and that the princes of the Church will bow their necks to the yoke.

42_marg2691: The Hebrews hand down that the Edomites were subject to Jehoshaphat king of Judah, and the Moabites to Joram king of Israel. But a little after, when the king of the Moabites had revolted from Joram, Joram asked help from Jehoshaphat king of Judah. He came and brought with him the king of the Edomites to besiege the city where the king of Moab was shut up; and when the king of Moab tried to flee from the city by the side that the king of the Edomites was besieging, he was not allowed to by him. Then, going up on the wall, he sacrificed his son to his god; and for the monstrousness of this crime the children of Israel withdrew from the city. Afterwards, when the king of the Edomites had died and been buried, the Moabites, remembering what he had done against them in the siege, dragged him out of the tomb and burnt him with fire and reduced him to ashes, so that what they could not do to him living, they might avenge on him dead.
42_marg2692: To show that all the souls he has created belong to his rule, God threatens to avenge on the Moabites the crime they committed against the king of the Edomites, in that they did not end their cruelty even at his death. 42_marg2693: Allegorically: The bones of the king of Edom are the most solid and firm spiritual understanding that lies within the letter. He burns the bones of the king of Edom who, thinking ill of the majesty of God, thinks of God after the manner of a human body, as though he were stretched out in limbs, and saw and heard like a man.

42_marg2700: The princes of the Jews had such customs as these: if a poor man joined them on the road, they flogged him and threw him on the dust of the earth, disdaining to walk with the simple. It also often happened among them that a son defiled his father’s wife, or again that a father defiled his son’s wife. Those too who would not go to worship the calves they killed or stripped, and, laying out pieces of their garments beside the altars of their gods, they reclined on them, and gave a part for wine, which they drank before the altars of the gods. This spoil is called a pledge, that is, a surety, because it was given for the killing of the body and the setting free of the soul. In all these things the name of the Lord is profaned. Whatever is done shamefully by them is turned to God’s dishonour, who says: “the name of God, through you, is blasphemed among the Gentiles.”

42_marg2703: The heretics, committing fornication under the Christian name, spread the testimonies of the Scriptures over their errors, not laying them under the Saviour’s footsteps, so that they may bear him witness, but covering their sins with them.
